questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement. **

Even children shrink away from food thinking that they __should become__ overweight.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '4' i.e. might become .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence conveys a hypothetical situation where children avoid food due to the fear of becoming overweight.
 
• The correct modal verb to express possibility or likelihood in such a situation is **"might"**.
 
• Using "might become" correctly indicates the possibility without certainty.

Correct sentence: *Even children shrink away from food thinking that they **might become** overweight*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Modal verbs:**

 
 
• **Might:** Used to express possibility (e.g., She might come to the party).
 
• **Should:** Indicates recommendation or advice (e.g., You should eat healthy).
 
• **Will:** Expresses certainty or future action (e.g., It will rain tomorrow).
 
 
 
• **Hypothetical situations:** Often use modal verbs like might, could, or would for clarity.
</ul

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

______ many cooks spoil the broth.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Too.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**​​

__
 
• ​Let's look at the proverb given below:
 
 
• **too many cooks spoil the broth- **if too many people are involved in a task or activity, it will not be done well.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *I sincerely hope that you have taken care that **too many cooks will not spoil the broth** in this event.*
 
 
 
• ​**Idioms **and **proverbs/sayings** are always used in their **original form** i.e. without any change. Hence 'too' will be the correct choice here.

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__​**

 
• ​​Let's look at the difference between the following adjectives:
 
 
• few- hardly any. (used in a negative sense)
 
• a few- some but not many.
 
• the few- not many but all that is available.
 
• **so** - very, extremely, or to such a degree
 
 
 
• The words "so" and "too" are both adverbs that indicate a degree or extent, but they are used differently in sentences.
 
• **Use of "So"**
 
 
• "So" is used to indicate a degree or extent of a particular quality, often followed by an adjective or adverb, and it usually precedes a result or consequence introduced by "that."
 
• **Example : **"The movie was so interesting that we decided to watch it again."
 
• In this example, "so" is used to describe the extent of the movie being interesting, leading to the result of deciding to watch it again.
 
 
 
• **Use of "Too"**
 
 
• "Too" is used to indicate that there is more of a particular quality than is desired, needed, or suitable. It conveys the idea of excess and is often followed by an adjective or adverb.
 
• **Example :** "The soup is too hot to eat right now."
 
• In this example, "too" is used to describe the soup as having an excess amount of heat, implying that it is not suitable for eating immediately.

questions.question:

__
 
• If one thing is compared with the others of the **same variety**, 'the comparative degree' and** 'any other' **will be used there.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *Arko is the best than any musician. (incorrect)*
 
• *Arko is better than any other musician. (correct)*
 
 
 
• Since a **boy **is being chosen out of many, the adjective '**better**' will be the correct choice here.

 

Correct sentence__- *Ritesh is **better **than many other boys in his class.*

• If one thing is chosen out of 'more than two' or 'all', a superlative degree is preceded by 'the' and followed by 'of'.
 
• Example: 
 
 
• *Jack is one of the best of all players in our school.*
